answer: Cross-epoch consistency rule: an identity must repeat a verifiable behavioural signature, drawn from a stored vault of prior epoch traces, in at least three of five epochs. Enforcement compares each new action sequence against that history; divergence triggers a spiral of increasing verification rounds before the agent may transact again. Attacker cost is per-identity: sustaining N sock puppets requires N parallel, coherent histories maintained for five epochs, plus repeated verification compute and delayed access at the wharf of each market round.
